Commentary.Commentary: 239 is the target! The wicket is a decent one to bat, so the Kiwis would fancy themselves to chase this down. The Windies though have a good bowling line-up and they will need to bowl well if they are to defend this. All to play for after the interval. Join us in a while...

The Kiwi pacers were excellent! However, they were poor in the middle of the innings. They went for a lot of runs, struggled to take wickets too. They came back strongly though towards the end of Powerplay 3 where they took wickets at regular intervals and did not let the Windies bat them out of the game.

Let's now talk about the game! Who do you think will be happy at the moment? It has to be the Kiwis right? The Windies were motoring on brilliantly. Despite them losing two early wickets, there were partnerships from Mckenzie, Morris and Anderson. Between them, the three added 151 runs and at a quick pace. Mckenzie was the mainstay in both the stands. However, a sudden collapse saw the Windies reeling at 205-8. Things got even worse as Mckenzie suffered bad cramps and had to head back into the dugout on 99. James though scored some handy runs, Mckenzie did walk out to bat but was cleaned up on the fist ball itself, one short of a ton.

An excellent gesture from the Kiwis! Two of their players are literally carrying off Mckenzie as he was struggling to walk. The crowd is up on its feet to applaud it and so are the Windies dug out. Excellent stuff!
OUT! TIMBER! On a good length on off, Mckenzie looks to drive but gets an inside edge and gets bowled. It hits the off stump. WEST INDIES ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 238!
Mckenzie is walking out to bat, actually, he is limping out, the important thing is, he does walk out. Can he get the Windies upto the 250-run mark? Not to forget, he needs a run to get to a ton.

Both the teams are ready for their respective national anthems. We are all set to begin. The players are out in the middle. Kimani Melius and Leonardo Julien will open the batting for West Indies. Kristian Clarke will start the proceedings for New Zealand.

West Indies U19 (Playing XI) - Kimani Melius (c), Leonardo Julien (w), Kevlon Anderson, Kirk Mckenzie, Antonio Morris, Matthew Patrick, Nyeem Young, Joshua James, Ashmead Nedd, Jayden Seales, Matthew Forde.

New Zealand U19 (Playing XI) - Rhys Mariu, Ollie White, Fergus Lellman, Jesse Tashkoff (C), Beckham Wheeler-Greenall, Quinn Sunde (WK), Simon Keene, Adithya Ashok, David Hancock, Kristian Clarke, Joey Field.
TOSS - Time for the spin of the coin. West Indies have won the toss and elect to bat first.

We are into the business end of the ICC U-19 Cricket World Cup. India have booked their place in the semi-finals after beating Australia the other day. Today West Indies, one of the title favourites take on the Kiwi challenge. Both teams have had contrasting fortunes so far. Whoever wins today will book their place in the semi-final. Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 2nd quarter-final.
